title: Scarborough Line: a shoal and a treaty
oneLine: China and the Philippines keep clashing at Scarborough Shoal; Washington says its 1951 treaty covers Philippine ships there, and Manila's politics are at war with themselves.

whoIsWho.stance: Leans on the US alliance and publicises Chinese pressure at sea.
Wants the shoal held and the US treaty left dormant, without a war.
Vice President on trial before the Senate; her camp wants a softer line on China.
The 1951 pact; Washington says an attack on Philippine vessels would trigger it.

whyItMatters: If China builds an island at Scarborough it gains a base 220 km from Manila, overlooking routes toward Taiwan. A fatal incident could test whether the US treaty means what Washington says.

timeline.text: The US and the Philippines sign their Mutual Defense Treaty.
A standoff ends with China in control of Scarborough Shoal.
A Hague tribunal rejects China's sweeping South China Sea claims.
Rodrigo Duterte is arrested and sent to the ICC.
Chinese and Philippine warships face off at the shoal.
Sara Duterte's Senate impeachment trial begins.
China's coast guard fires water cannon on Philippine ships.
